scope: Final visible draft, deployed JSON, exact article/action blobs, authenticated rendered prose and links, independent-review lifecycle and canonical binding, open-PR counts, October 21 acceptance provenance, action ownership, generator timing, executable next steps, and authority boundaries. Read-only review; no acceptance, action, workflow, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: Completed independent reviews are described as unfinished model pipelines
findings.location: Independent-review decision, roadmap pulse, and first suggested action, lines 23–25, 45–51, and 75–78.
findings.explanation: PRs #421, #433, #449 and #450 already contain completed source-pinned review records, validations, open findings and agent handoffs. None exposes an outstanding proposer/verifier pass, receipt queue, readiness promotion or label transition. The creation gaps for #449 and #450 also contradict the claim that reviews open as soon as publication is visible.
findings.correction: Describe these as completed proposed review records awaiting supervised finding disposition and a decision whether to request source corrections. Remove the model-pass, receipt-queue, promotion and stall narrative.

findings.title: PR descriptions are not the canonical review records
findings.location: Hash-pinning decision and draft context, lines 29–31 and 78.
findings.explanation: The service validates the registered JSON, article at its source commit, article blob and full-record blob, while treating the PR body as correspondence. The schema carries those pins in the registered record and defines no proposer/verifier pass identity.
findings.correction: Identify registered JSON plus verified full-record Markdown and article blob as the canonical binding. Treat the PR description only as a summary/correspondence surface.

findings.title: Open draft and repository counts are wrong
findings.explanation: The current inventory has eight drafts across three repositories: four daily-logger reviews, classic-space-venue #8, and LEGO #44–#46. Morning-cockpit #60 is open but not draft, so including its repository does not produce seven drafts across four repositories.
findings.correction: Report eight draft PRs across three repositories, or ten open PRs across four repositories if counting the two non-drafts. Name the population explicitly.

findings.title: October 21 acceptance is attributed to the review-registration PR
findings.explanation: Acceptance PR #416 merged the Accepted article. PR #447 later registered the final review. The final record preserves a partial outcome with all three suggestions still Needs review, Opus not reached and no action admissions or closures; it measures 3 days, 2 hours, 53 minutes from initial review opening to acceptance.
findings.correction: Attribute acceptance to #416 and review registration to #447, retain the partial action outcome, and use the measured interval instead of a five-day acceptance claim.

findings.title: A gcgcca roadmap action is assigned to capture-agent
findings.location: Capture-agent milestones, draft context, and second suggested action, lines 67–68 and 75–78.
findings.explanation: The canonical registry assigns act-2026-07-31-adr-61a759 to capture-agent for the codegen ADR, but assigns act-2026-04-07-roadmap-6f4599 to gcgcca for its Module Federation remote at :3035. The latter is not a capture-agent ADR or milestone.
findings.correction: Keep the two records under their actual repositories and scopes; do not combine them into one capture-agent dependency or status command.

findings.title: Steady-state framing hides a late fallback dispatch
findings.location: Title, summary, introduction, and What shipped, lines 3, 6, and 11–17.
findings.explanation: Run #271 was workflow_dispatch at 04:59:07 Chicago, 5,347 seconds after the declared 03:30 trigger. PR #451 merged at 05:08:26 Chicago. These receipts establish a late fallback-dispatch path and merge, not native scheduled creation or by-04:00 public availability.
findings.correction: Qualify the run as fallback-dispatched and separate declared trigger, actual start, merge and observed public availability. Do not use it as schedule steady-state evidence.

findings.title: Proposed review-status and ADR-status commands do not exist
findings.explanation: Pinned scripts, workflows and source expose neither /review-draft-status nor /adr-status. The first asks about nonexistent outstanding review-model passes; the second joins differently owned canonical actions. Both candidates remain awaiting-review and are not admitted or dispatchable.
findings.correction: Use plain source-backed recommendations on the real PR and action surfaces instead of invented command syntax.

findings.title: Human-read ordering and a deliberate latency tradeoff are unproved
findings.explanation: Publication and review PR timestamps establish ordering, but the checked sources do not authenticate the first human read or record a design decision choosing publish latency over review-before-publish integrity. The gaps before #449 and #450 opened leave human-read ordering unknown.
findings.correction: Report only that publication preceded these independent-review PRs. Attribute human-read timing or a deliberate optimization only to a primary decision or authenticated receipt.
